decisions.decision: How should incoming documents be scored?
decisions.context: The system classifies millions of documents per day, and volume changes seasonally. The brief does not specify a response-time target.

alternatives.label: Queue-fronted online serving cluster
pros: High throughput: queue distributes scoring load
cons: Shared results: requires a separate results store

alternatives.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
pros: High throughput: scores documents in batches
Shared results: writes results to storage
cons: Seasonal volume: batch capacity must be scheduled
Freshness: results wait for the next run

decisions.rationale: High throughput decides the choice: the queue distributes scoring across predictors and absorbs bursts, as described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “System Architectures for Personalization and Recommendation.” This gives up batch simplicity; the brief does not establish a latency target.
consequences: Operate a queue and scale predictor capacity with backlog.
Persist results for multiple consuming teams.

decisions.decision: How should runtime capacity respond to seasonal demand?
decisions.context: Classification demand varies strongly over the year, so fixed capacity risks either insufficient peak capacity or unused off-peak resources.

alternatives.label: Elastic resource scaling
pros: Seasonal volume: capacity follows workload demand

alternatives.label: Scale-to-zero serving
cons: Seasonal volume: cold starts may slow resumed scoring

decisions.rationale: Seasonal volume decides the choice: elastic resources adjust to workload demand, as described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture.” This gives up some cost simplicity because scaling behavior needs tuning.
consequences: Monitor workload and capacity to tune scaling.
Peak throughput depends on available infrastructure.

decisions.decision: How should classification quality drift be detected?
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. The design space treats monitoring practices as combinable, so use input drift signals alongside measured prediction quality when labels become available.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring + real-time prediction-quality monitoring
pros: Drift visibility: flags changing inputs and schemas
Quality feedback: measures predictions when labels arrive
cons: Quality feedback: waits for labeled examples
Operations: requires monitoring both inputs and predictions

alternatives.label: Passive production operation
cons: Quality feedback: failures may remain unnoticed

chosen.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring + real-time prediction-quality monitoring

decisions.rationale: Drift visibility decides the choice: input monitoring can reveal changes before delayed labels arrive, while prediction-quality monitoring checks outcomes once labels are available. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Machine Learning Monitoring: What It Is, and What We Are Missing” describe these monitoring practices; the trade-off is added monitoring work and delayed quality feedback.
consequences: Retain inputs and predictions for monitoring and later evaluation.
Define alert thresholds and a response process.

uncovered: The LLM model, provider, and inference-cost strategy.
Document ingestion, retries, deduplication, and ordering guarantees.
The result contract, persistence, and access controls for consuming teams.
Label collection and evaluation policy for delayed quality measurement.
Data privacy, retention, and security requirements.
